data.narrative:
Neura Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Reger, has raised $1.4B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 same-stage, same-sector private comparables (Hadrian at $1.6B, Agile Robots and Nimble Robotics each at $1.0B) plus reference to a broader universe of 8 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yields $2.4B. The Peer-Median method anchors to the median valuation of the 3-company comparable set at $1.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. These approaches reflect different assumptions about capital efficiency and peer positioning.

Triangulation across both methods produces a range of $850M (downside) to $2.7B (upside), with a median of $1.7B. The wide dispersion reflects uncertainty around whether Neura Robotics commands a premium to the peer median or aligns with stage-typical progression. Key variables include relative capital efficiency, revenue or unit traction relative to peers, and the company's specific technical differentiation within the robotics sector.
